sections.h2: Selling in Cheektowaga without a long listing
sections.html:
Anyone selling in Cheektowaga can list with an agent, go without one, or take an offer directly from a buyer like us. Going direct appeals to owners who would rather not fix things, stage rooms or wait on a lender, and you pick the closing day.

Cheektowaga is a town in Erie County and the second-largest suburb of Buffalo after Amherst. It contains the village of Sloan and half of the village of Depew. The rules that apply to your house can differ depending on whether it lies in the town outside the villages, so look at your tax bill first.

An estimated 88,160 people lived in town in mid-2025, below the 89,877 counted in the 2020 census and above the 88,226 of 2010. Homes are affordable by regional standards: the median owner's home is worth $185,000, against $164,200 in Buffalo and $332,700 nationwide. With 19.7% of residents at 65 or older, a good number of local sales come from estates and older owners moving to smaller places.

Most of the housing was built in the postwar subdivision boom of the 1950s and 1960s. A buyer's inspector will therefore look hard at the heating, the electrical panel and the age of the shingles. After lake-effect winters, a roof patched more than once or a basement that takes on water in the spring thaw can push a repair estimate past what a seller wants to spend. Selling as is passes that job to the buyer.

Cheektowaga borders Buffalo on the west, Amherst on the north, Lancaster on the east and West Seneca on the south. Several of its neighborhoods have their own school districts.

  • Bellevue, between Union Road and the Depew line
  • Cleveland Hill, on the north town line, with its own school district
  • Maryvale, west of the airport, which is also a school district
  • Pine Hill, on the Buffalo border near Villa Maria College
  • Doyle, South Line and U-Crest in the south and southwest
  • Sloan, a village and the seat of the Cheektowaga-Sloan school district

Eight separate public school districts operate inside the town, so a buyer's first question is often which one covers the house. Boundaries follow the parcel, so ask the district itself before answering. Buffalo Niagara International Airport lies within the town, and the New York State Thruway, I-90, crosses it from north to south. Union Road (NY 277), Harlem Road (NY 240), Transit Road (NY 78) and Broadway (NY 130) carry local traffic, with the Kensington Expressway (NY 33) and I-190 leading toward Buffalo.

If you own property in the town outside the villages of Sloan and Depew and you do not live there, you must register it. Chapter 194 of the town code, the Landlord Rental and Property Owner Registration Ordinance, requires registration every two years whether the building is occupied or vacant.

  • The registration fee is $20.
  • New owners file a registration statement within 30 days of buying.
  • Failing to register violates section 194-6 and carries a fine.

With a rental or an inherited house that sits empty, bring the registration up to date before closing. The town's Building Department covers building, plumbing, fire safety and neighborhood preservation, and the Town Clerk and Receiver of Taxes publishes the registration page. Buyers' lawyers sometimes ask for proof, and a lapsed registration costs less to fix now than at the closing table.

Deeds for Cheektowaga houses are recorded by the Erie County Clerk. The seller pays transfer tax when the TP-584 goes in: $2.00 per $500 of price to the state plus $2.50 per $500 to the county, or $4.50 per $500 in all. A seller aged 62 or older who has owned and lived in a one- or two-family house for at least a year can lower the rate to $2.00 per $500 by signing an affidavit, which the County Clerk's office provides free.

A 1% Mansion Tax applies once the price on a residential conveyance reaches $1 million. Home sales come with a separate Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form. The clerk's office cannot help fill out legal forms, so a lawyer or title agent normally drafts the documents and handles the filing.

The Cheektowaga Assessment Office, phone 716-686-3440, can confirm your assessed value, and the town website posts the tentative and final assessment rolls. Before you sell, ask whether your parcel has an exemption on file. A buyer who takes over the house may need to apply for their own, and knowing what is in place now avoids a surprise on the first tax bill.

sections.h2: First steps for a Cheektowaga seller
sections.html:
Cheektowaga sales often involve an older house with years of deferred upkeep, a rental the owner no longer wants to manage, or an inherited home. Each of those has its own paperwork, and handling it in the right order saves time.

Walk through the house with a notebook before you call anyone. Note the roof, the furnace, the water heater, any basement dampness and the windows, and write down which repairs you have already paid for. A direct buyer will want these details, and having them ready gets you a firmer first offer.

Four items keep a quick sale on track.

  • Confirm from the deed and tax bill whether the house is in the town outside the villages or inside Sloan or Depew.
  • Register the property with the town if you do not live in it, and pay the $20 fee.
  • Request a payoff letter from your lender, and check with the Assessment Office on any exemptions.
  • Gather the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 so the Erie County Clerk can record the transfer at closing.

Owners live in 71.5% of homes here, so most sellers are individual homeowners rather than investors. A direct buyer can build the closing around a mortgage payoff, a probate timeline or your move date. For a house left by a parent, gather the death certificate and the papers showing who has authority to sell, since the title company will ask for them. Tell the buyer which of those applies, and the schedule can be set around it. If a family member needs to sign, arrange that early, since an out-of-town heir is a common cause of delay.

faqs.q: Is Cheektowaga a city or a town?
faqs.a: It is a town in Erie County. It contains the village of Sloan and half of the village of Depew, and it sits next to Buffalo on the city's east side.

faqs.q: What does Cheektowaga charge to register a non-owner-occupied house?
faqs.a: The fee is $20. Registration repeats every two years, and the first statement is due within 30 days after you buy.

faqs.q: Is there a senior discount on Cheektowaga transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Erie County allows owners aged 62 or older to reduce the rate from $4.50 to $2.00 per $500 if they owned and lived in a one- or two-family home for at least a year before the sale. The County Clerk's office hands out the affidavit at no charge.
The town Assessment Office, reachable at 716-686-3440. Its website also carries the tentative and final assessment rolls.

faqs.q: Which school district serves a given Cheektowaga house?
faqs.a: Eight public districts operate within the town, among them Cheektowaga-Sloan, Maryvale and Cleveland Hill. The answer depends on the parcel, so verify with the district before telling a buyer.
